question.text: Commodity cycles are driven primarily by:

answer.text: Changes in government fiscal policy alone
Supply-demand imbalances in physical commodity markets

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes commodity cycles as driven by supply-demand dynamics: prices rise with increased demand, fall when suppliers add capacity, and rise again when supply decreases. The cycle is therefore driven by physical supply-demand imbalances. The Trap: Fiscal policy alone and stock-market sentiment alone are too narrow as drivers, and accounting standards do not move commodity cycles. Note: Commodity cycles often follow economic cycles and can also occur independently through demand, capacity and supply adjustments, as covered on pages 102-103 of the NISM-Series-XV Research Analyst Certification Examination workbook (February 2026).
